source_text: Yes, that's an excellent idea, to use the R-nodes as internal factors, since we've already done the analysis of its adjacency matrix, indeed, our work has somewhat turned Friston's physics into a physics-inspired ontology, though it's an "abstract ontology" rather than a lexical one.  And because AIF is what it is, the system is somewhat scale free.  So, "we bring food to your house" scales up to "the trade deficit with Mexico" or whatever.

reply_text:
I've found the War Machine wiring matrix (`M-wm-wiring/wm-adjacency.edn`). Now I'm writing the R-nodes-as-internal-factors section with a worked example of delivery at three scales.㊥ (gist) I've added §3.5 to the mission (`59c299e`). It treats the R-nodes as the internal factors of each scattering and works one example at three scales: food to your house, a city's restaurant-delivery market, and the food trade deficit with Mexico.

🈖 ("an "abstract ontology" rather than a lexical one") Two ontologies now meet in the mission. The SVO triples are the lexical side: what people say they intend. The R-nodes are the abstract side: the factors any scattering passes through. The §3.1 fit joins them, for example delegate → R10, verify by a second process → R9, constrain spend → R11. The abstract side lives in three places:
- `futon3c/holes/labs/M-wm-wiring/wm-adjacency.edn` (the wiring matrix)
- `futon2/.../aif-equations.edn` (the 37-edge equation DAG)
- the R1–R16 pattern map

㊢ ("scales up to "the trade deficit with Mexico"") The three-scale table keeps the same rows (o, C, π/G, R11, R9, out-channels) at every size, and I think it bears out your claim of scale-freedom. What changes as you scale up is the C row. At the household level the preference is "hungry, cheap, now". At the national level it's food security against farm incomes against consumer prices, held by two governments and farmers on both sides. That ties back to §3.4, where the human problems sat where several parties' preferences meet. So in War Machine terms, the scale-free part is the form. The difficulty grows with the number of people setting R19 and how far apart they are.

㊟ (honest status) Using the R-nodes as an ontology doesn't need the wires to work. Using the War Machine as a *model* of a particular client does, and the PROOF-2a log shows the matrix at 104 wires with none verified live as of 09-26. I've noted that in the section so the two claims don't get mixed up.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: (gist) The scattering picture works for this. It gives a test for every tool on the list: does it change what comes out, or only how things bounce around inside? I've recorded it in the mission as §3.3 (`7ca2b4d`).

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: ("is it on the way to solving real human needs better or faster?") In scattering theory the internal detail matters only through what comes out. A tool earns its place if you can trace a path from the bounce it changes to a change in an out-state. By that test, most of group A (Mastra, Smithers, the memory databases) improves bounces. Whether that ever reaches anyone's dinner depends on the factory around it, and the tool alone can't tell you.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: (DoorDash) The example adds one thing: there's more than one out-channel. The customer gets food: how fast, how cheap, whether it's the right order. The same process also has out-channels for couriers (pay, hours) and for restaurants (margin). Extra tech inside can make the customer's channel better or faster while making the couriers' worse. So "better for whom?" has to be part of how the out-state is described.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: (a case already in the data) The customer-stories research has an example where the bounces cancel out. Judgment Labs' clients found that reviewing the agent's output took up the time the agent had saved. Each step was carried out faithfully, and nothing changed at the output. So fidelity at each step, in the T8 sense, doesn't add up to an end-to-end gain.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: (War Machine) In this picture the R-nodes are internal bounces. "Grounded in how an organisation works" would then mean the War Machine's observations (R2) come from the organisation's out-channels, not from its own internal steps. That's a test you could apply to the current validation work.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(next) When the remaining customer-story agents report back, I'll write each client problem in this form:
- the in-state, as the client states it
- the out-channels, and who is on each one
- a measurable out-state for each channel
- which bounces each tool touches
